subject: Split billing and automated VAT-ID validation for multi-entity supply
messages:
From: Sophie Marchand <sophie@cloudarc.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Split billing + VAT-ID validation for multi-entity customers

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — quick context: CloudArc sells via a managed marketplace and we have two frequent situations causing invoicing and tax headaches:

1) B2B EU buyers with valid VAT IDs where reverse-charge should apply (buyer self-accounting).
2) Reseller flows where we (CloudArc) are a reseller and need to issue self-billed invoices to end customers while paying out platform fees to third parties.

We need a robust, automated approach that:
- Validates VAT IDs at onboarding and periodically (ideally VIES + fallback).
- Automatically marks invoice lines for reverse-charge vs standard VAT based on buyer_vat_valid / supply_type.
- Splits invoices so platform fees (subject to place-of-supply rules) and payout lines are separately tagged for tax reporting and nettling.

Can Redwood propose a concrete mapping (invoice line fields + tax treatment rules) we can plug into our accounting export? Also attaching a small sample CSV of recent invoice lines so you can see our columns.

Attachments: sample-invoice-CloudArc.csv (csv, 1MB)

We'd like a short proposal and an estimate for implementation effort and any feature flags we should enable in the console. If helpful, happy to schedule a 30m sync.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Marchand
Head of Finance Operations
CloudArc Ltd

CloudArc Billing <billing@cloudarc.com>
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Split billing + VAT-ID validation for multi-entity customers

Thanks Sophie — useful sample, and good call to automate. High-level proposal below; I'll attach a short PDF with the mapping and an implementation timeline.

Summary proposal (short):
- VAT-ID validation: on-create + nightly re-validation. Primary: VIES lookup; fallback: checksum + manual queue if VIES returns unknown or rate-limited. Store confidence: high|medium|low.
- Invoice model: we add structured invoice-line metadata: {line_id, supply_type, buyer_vat_number, buyer_country, place_of_supply, tax_treatment, source_entity, payout_entity}.
- Automatic tax rule evaluation: tax_treatment values: reverse_charge | standard_vat | zero_rated | out_of_scope. Rules driven by buyer_vat_valid, supply_type (service/goods/platform_fee), and buyer_country vs seller_entity_country.
- Split billing: platform fee lines emitted as separate invoice rows with payout_entity tag; ledger export includes a grouping key so your accounting system can net payouts vs platform revenue.
- Self-billing / reseller: support self-billed invoice flag which triggers a different presentation and optional route for customer approvals.
- Audit evidence: store VIES response snapshot + timestamp and include a link in the invoice PDF for auditors.

Operational notes:
- We recommend caching VIES results for 72h and a manual review queue for low-confidence IDs.
- Provide an API/webhook for VAT-ID validation events (validation_passed/validation_failed) that you can consume in onboarding flows.
- For volume above ~50k lookups/month we can discuss batch validation pricing and local cache nodes to avoid VIES rate limits.

Next steps:
1) I attached a 2-page PDF with field mappings and a 3-week implementation estimate for Dedicated customers; hosted rollout may be faster.
2) Ben: can you add notes re: batching/Optimize impact and any console flags?
3) Sophie: if you can share monthly volume and top 5 countries we'll refine the cost/latency plan.

Attachments: vat-automation-proposal.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Billing
Redwood Inference

Adding a few practical constraints from an Optimize/ops perspective:
- VIES caching: agree with 72h TTL, but we should tier TTL by confidence and country (some VAT authorities are more stable).
- Batch jobs: provide an on-demand bulk-validate job (CSV in, validation report out) — CloudArc can drop nightly files to an S3 bucket and we'll process.
- Cost/latency: real-time validation on checkout adds ~120-250ms depending on cache hit; recommend async validation for high-volume checkouts with a soft-block flow if confidence is low.
- Rate limits: we should set soft-rate thresholds per account and surface metrics in console.

Ben notes / asks for Sophie:
- Monthly invoice volume? (approx)
- Top 5 buyer countries
- Do you need real-time Distributed Ledger tags for your GL or is a daily export ok?

Also linking the HubSpot ticket where I've added an R&D task for local cache nodes: https://app.hubspot.com/tickets/6789012
And the DPA/DocuSign we use for EU tax tooling: https://docusign.com/link/abc123
